EXP-ret-tight.title: Retriever comparison — which retrieval method finds valid recipes
EXP-ret-tight.desc: Compares retrieval methods on their ability to surface constraint-valid recipes for a persona (tight stratum, n=1,646). Headline: lightweight symbolic retrieval (Text→Pandas) reaches hit@10 ≈ 0.43 with a GPT-4o-mini backbone and ≈ 0.85 with Llama-70B — about 8–15× the best embedding retriever (dense 0.055) — at a fraction of the cost of agentic graph traversal.

EXP-7.title: Full system matrix + baselines — FoodRAG vs the baseline ladder
EXP-7.desc: FoodRAG's four system configurations (H1 agentic / H2 recommend-only × dense / Text→Pandas) against the baseline ladder (popularity, LLM-only, naive-RAG, ToG). Headline: an unconstrained LLM violates a hard allergen constraint 90.5% of the time; FoodRAG's deterministic safety filter drives allergen violations to 0.000 across all configs, and the agentic H1-t2p is the best config overall (correctness 0.765).

EXP-5.title: Knowledge-graph retrieval — feasibility on the tight stratum
EXP-5.desc: Real knowledge-graph retrieval run, tight stratum only (n=12, small_1). Broad-stratum KG retrieval is infeasible without precomputation (Protocol §5.5). Framed as a feasibility demonstration, not a retriever bake-off.

EXP-10k.title: Popularity baselines — the popularity-bias reference
EXP-10k.desc: Popularity-sorted baselines across answer-set strata. Health-aware popularity (0b) pre-filters to the constraint-valid set before ranking, so it trivially hits — a reference ceiling that 'knows the answer key', not a competitor. Raw popularity shows the popularity-bias story: high relevance, low health.

EXP-10k-tight.title: LLM-only & naive-RAG baselines (tight stratum)
EXP-10k-tight.desc: The core justification for retrieval/grounding: an unconstrained LLM-only baseline invents recipes that break a hard allergen constraint 90.5% of the time. Naive-RAG grounds the answer and collapses that to <1%.

EXP-10k-tog.title: ToG — agentic knowledge-graph traversal baseline
EXP-10k-tog.desc: Think-on-Graph agentic KG traversal. Competent (hit@10 ≈ 0.41) but ~903 s/item — heavy agentic traversal buys less than Text→Pandas at ~50× the cost.
